Supported/reported mode remains distinct from lifecycle state and health. No new mode row is needed.

The existing delegated/independent path candidate covers manager/agent, direct/indirect and in-/out-of-band roles. Clarify whether the component is managed or unmanaged; a missing endpoint does not prove absence of indirect management.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Interface boundary, kind and governing context
new_candidates.definition: An interface is described relative to a named system boundary: internal interfaces remain within it, while external interfaces cross it. Preserve physical versus logical context, the interacting subjects or environment, and any stated open, closed or standardized interface context. C239 external interfaces include the sensing aperture toward the environment as well as host connections. Boundary crossing does not establish separate equipment, an installed cable, a network endpoint or a universal sensor boundary.
new_candidates.reason: Physical membership and connected equipment do not express interface locality relative to a specified boundary; an environment-facing aperture need not connect to a separate device. A generic relation is a possible carrier, but does not already state this information need. Common: boundary-qualified interfaces apply across equipment arrangements without adopting SOSA geometry or a universal chassis.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Logical functions and implementation allocation
new_candidates.definition: Describe a logical function or role separately from the hardware, firmware, software and runtime infrastructure that implements or supports it. A procurable unit can combine several functions and infrastructure elements; a logical module need not equal one physical part, runtime or purchased unit. Retain the declared grouping and implementation relationship without imposing one-to-one cardinality. C239 module names are source vocabulary, not a mandatory class list or proof of installed functionality.
new_candidates.reason: An ISA network service/required-command role, a capability catalogue, physical membership and runtime settings each describe only part of this distinction. Generic relations can carry allocation but do not explicitly identify the logical function, realizing infrastructure and procurement grouping. Common: preserve function-versus-realization across donors without adopting SOSA decomposition.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Scoped conformance or qualification claim and verification basis
new_candidates.definition: Keep a conformance, certification or qualification claim tied to its subject, applicable standard or requirement, covered interfaces/aspects and stated verification basis. Distinguish a certificate from a method such as analysis, inspection, demonstration or test, and distinguish environmental qualification from airworthiness. A conformant component or interface does not establish whole-system conformance. No certificate, equipment test result or external certification-policy audit was obtained here.
new_candidates.reason: Generic assertions carry provenance but do not name the scope and verification basis of a conformity claim. Standard lifecycle standing, a product category and a built-in-test result answer different questions. Common: qualified compliance/verification information is transferable; SOSA certification rules and aviation qualification remain source-qualified, not universal DIM obligations.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Subject-qualified security assessment state
new_candidates.definition: Describe the assessed security posture of a specified system, card or software module from the reporting manager’s perspective, with its policy/assessment context. C239 system states Evaluating, Protected, Degraded and Compromised differ from PIC states Trust Pending, Trusted and Untrusted and the separately described software authentication states. Security state is parallel to operational state and can constrain operation; it is not a certificate, key-filled flag or proof that equipment is safe or authenticated. Preserve each native subject and state vocabulary.
new_candidates.reason: Credential trust, operational condition, mode, key presence and tamper alerts do not represent a manager’s assessment of system/component security posture. Common: security assessment with subject and provenance is transferable; do not universalize the C239 enumerations or infer successful authentication.
locators: §6.5.4 PDF136–138; retained B-26 scope corrected against original prose

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Reported data-product processing stage
new_candidates.definition: Preserve whether an output is described as raw or minimally processed Data Products or processed/reduced Information Products in its source context. This qualifies the product’s processing stage, separately from a detection method, observation identity and links between an original event and digital copies. C239 supplies a coarse distinction, not a universal processing-level scale, detailed algorithm lineage or verified processing history.
new_candidates.reason: An output field, event-generation method and original/copy lineage do not state the coarse processing stage of the delivered product. new_candidates.label: Candidate — Reported health assessment and associated faults
new_candidates.definition: A reported assessment describes the current or projected condition and well-being of a sensor, component or management function, with its assessed subject and any associated fault collection. C239 declares health and fault retrievals; their detailed 2023 object schemas, a universal health vocabulary and an actual equipment assessment are not established here.
new_candidates.reason: Operating-condition comparisons currently emphasize operational state; a generic property report is only a carrier. Health/well-being, including projected condition and faults, needs explicit representation separate from operational state and security. Common: the subject-qualified assessment is reusable without imposing a SOSA state vocabulary.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Health and security monitoring settings
new_candidates.definition: Describe the current parameter settings used by a specified health-monitoring or security-status-reporting function, including the health of a logger when that is the managed subject. These settings differ from the assessed condition, notification settings and capability readiness. C239 marks health-setting reads V1.0, most health-setting updates Future, logger-health updates V1.0, and security-status setting functions Future. No parameter fields, thresholds or implemented endpoints are inferred from the table names.
new_candidates.reason: A property declaration, readiness flag or assessed condition does not state the configuration of the monitoring function itself. Publication thresholds cannot stand in for all health/security monitoring settings. Common at the function/settings level; exact parameter structure remains outside the verified source scope.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Management notification settings
new_candidates.definition: Describe settings governing health, state, mode, configuration or security notifications for a specified sensor, component or management function. Keep notification configuration separate from a notification occurrence and its acknowledgment lifecycle, and from the monitored condition. C239 lists ordinary alert-setting functions as V1.0 and security-alert settings as Future; it does not establish that every setting is an absolute/relative threshold or expose their precise schema in these tables.
new_candidates.reason: Specific publication thresholds and alert lifecycle records do not explicitly describe the broader settings of a notification function. The source does not justify equating those settings to per-capability reporting selection. Common: retain managed subject and notification purpose, with exact setting vocabulary held.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Diagnostic test configuration
new_candidates.definition: Describe the parameter settings for a built-in diagnostic test of a sensor or component, separately from requesting the test and reporting its outcome. C239 names BITConfig retrieval/update interactions but marks all eight supporting function/interaction records Future. This is a provisional information need from an explicit planned function, not evidence of a current native endpoint, an available test suite or verified settings.
new_candidates.reason: The diagnostic command and result already have rows; neither records the test configuration. Declared command input syntax also differs from retrievable current test settings. Common as a reusable diagnostic-configuration need, with Future-only source standing explicit and no invented configuration fields.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Health log records and managed history
new_candidates.definition: Describe a retained health log for a sensor or its components, containing records about past, current or projected condition. C239 lists filtered LogEvent retrieval and deletion of selected log portions as V1.0, while log sanitization is Future. Keep retained health history separate from the latest condition, an operating-state-only history, security/accountability audit records and an archive-transfer request. No retention period, complete history, successful deletion or actual log contents are established.
new_candidates.reason: Current status, operating-state history, message-query commands and security audit records do not explicitly preserve the subject and purpose of health-history records. Common: one health-log need includes its managed history; retrieval/deletion operations remain qualified control interfaces rather than extra data rows.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Health logging configuration
new_candidates.definition: Describe configuration settings for the health logging function of a sensor. C239 separately declares LoggerConfiguration retrieval and update as V1.0. The logger configuration is distinct from the log records, the logger own health assessment and the parameters used to monitor that health. No retention, storage, filtering or export setting is assumed without its native definition.
new_candidates.reason: Publication triggers, subscription options, Status intervals and capability/readiness declarations do not define the settings of the health-recording function. Common: logging configuration is useful across equipment while its native fields remain unverified.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Firmware or software package and target component
new_candidates.definition: Associate a firmware/software package with its target component and distinguish information identifying the package reported as running from a package submitted for replacement. C239 declares package-information retrieval and replacement as V1.0, and package verification as Future with authenticity verification assigned to Security Services. Package identity is not merely a version string or an exchange-package ID. No native package fields, authentic image, successful installation or observed running instance are established.
new_candidates.reason: A running-software version, deployment configuration and generic file/package association do not explicitly preserve the package-to-target relationship and its reported-running versus replacement-input role. Common: preserve those roles without imposing SOSA packaging or treating an update request as successful deployment.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Resource inventory and reservation state
new_candidates.definition: Describe resources associated with a hardware element, logical module or runtime environment and their reported reservation status. C239 identifies resource-list retrieval, reservation request/grant-or-denial, release by reservation ID and a cryptographic-resource list. All seven supporting records are Future. Preserve resource, reservation and request roles without inventing capacities, scheduling, lease duration, exclusivity or current implementation.
new_candidates.reason: Exclusive command access concerns control of a component, while these reservations concern hardware/module/runtime resources. Runtime deployment and capability dependencies do not record current resource reservation. Common at the resource/reservation relationship level; Future-only standing and unspecified resource schemas remain explicit.

new_candidates.label: Candidate — Reported equipment and security configuration settings
new_candidates.definition: Describe a reported set of user-modifiable settings and their values for a sensor or component, including the separately scoped aggregate security configuration. Keep actual/reported settings separate from capability declarations, readiness selections, a configuration revision and an update request. C239 ordinary configuration reads/change notifications are V1.0; configuration updates and verification, and the security configuration functions, are Future. Verification may concern authenticity or suitability for a context/mode; no complete configuration schema, accepted configuration or physical application is established.
new_candidates.reason: ISA Config describes capabilities/readiness, and a version or retrieval command does not contain the configuration settings themselves. Generic named-property carriers cannot substitute for an explicit settings-set information need. Common: retain subject, settings and reported-versus-requested context without equating every donor configuration format.
